slides.heading: Spaghetti are long on purpose.
paragraphs: Cutting them with a knife turns a plate of pasta into a crime scene. Twirl them with your fork — that's the whole point.
Cut them in front of an Italian and expect a silence longer than the spaghetti.

slides.heading: Leave the spoon alone.
paragraphs: Twirling against a spoon is how kids learn. Adults use just the fork, against the side of the plate.
Yes, some restaurants abroad give you one. No, nonna does not approve.

slides.heading: The technique
items: Pick up just a few — not half the plate.
Twirl against the side of the plate, not in mid-air.
If it doesn't fit in one bite, you took too much. Start again.

slides.heading: Toddlers are forgiven.
paragraphs: Small children get their spaghetti cut. Everyone else gets judged.

slides.title: Save it before your next pasta.
slides.text: Follow for Italian Rule Nº 4 — the one about “pepperoni”. You've been lied to.

caption:
Italian Rule Nº 3 🍝
Never cut your spaghetti.

No knife. No spoon. Just a fork, a few strands and the side of the plate. It takes practice — Italians have had a few centuries of it.

Be honest: knife, spoon, or fork only? 👇

—
🇮🇹 Regola italiana n.3: gli spaghetti non si tagliano. Mai. Conoscete qualcuno che lo fa? Taggatelo.
